note: Key moments in Edmonton Oilers history. Every entry links to its source.

eras.name: Decade of Darkness & the Lottery Years

entries.title: Gretzky arrives in Edmonton
entries.text: The WHA Oilers acquire teenager Wayne Gretzky from the Indianapolis Racers in a deal that also brings Peter Driscoll and Eddie Mio to Edmonton.

entries.title: Into the NHL
entries.text: The NHL votes to admit four WHA clubs (Edmonton, Winnipeg, Quebec and Hartford) for the 1979-80 season, growing the league to 21 teams.

entries.title: A franchise-making first draft
entries.text: Edmonton's first NHL draft class includes Kevin Lowe (21st overall), Mark Messier (48th) and Glenn Anderson (69th), all future Hall of Famers.

entries.title: First NHL game
entries.text: The Oilers open their NHL life with a 4-2 loss at Chicago. Kevin Lowe scores the first goal in franchise NHL history.

entries.title: Stunning the Canadiens
entries.text: The young Oilers sweep Montreal 3-0 in the preliminary round (6-3, 3-1, 6-2) for their first NHL playoff series win.

entries.title: 50 goals in 39 games
entries.text: Gretzky scores five times in a 7-5 win over Philadelphia, reaching 50 goals in the Oilers' 39th game of the season.

entries.title: 92 goals, 212 points
entries.text: Gretzky finishes with an NHL-record 92 goals and 212 points, and wins the Hart Trophy unanimously with all 63 first-place votes.

entries.title: 446 goals
entries.text: The Oilers score 446 goals in 80 games (5.58 per game), the most by any team in a single NHL season.

entries.title: Cup No. 1
entries.text: Edmonton beats the Islanders 5-2 in Game 5 at Northlands Coliseum to win its first Stanley Cup. Mark Messier wins the Conn Smythe Trophy.

entries.title: Cup No. 2
entries.text: An 8-3 win over Philadelphia in Game 5 makes it back-to-back championships. Gretzky wins the Conn Smythe.

entries.title: Coffey passes Orr
entries.text: Paul Coffey breaks Bobby Orr's record of 46 goals by a defenceman and finishes 1985-86 with 48, still the NHL single-season mark.

entries.title: 215 points
entries.text: Gretzky sets NHL single-season records that still stand: 163 assists and 215 points (52 goals) in 80 games.

entries.title: Cup No. 3
entries.text: The Oilers win Game 7 of the Final 3-1 over Philadelphia in Edmonton.

entries.title: Cup No. 4
entries.text: After Game 4 in Boston is suspended at 3-3 by a power failure, Edmonton beats the Bruins 6-3 at home to finish a sweep. Gretzky wins his second Conn Smythe.

entries.title: The Trade
entries.text: Gretzky, Marty McSorley and Mike Krushelnyski go to Los Angeles for Jimmy Carson, Martin Gelinas, three first-round picks and $15 million.

entries.title: Gretzky passes Howe, in Edmonton
entries.text: Playing for the Kings at Northlands Coliseum, Gretzky ties the game with 53 seconds left for point No. 1,851, passing Gordie Howe as the NHL's all-time scoring leader.

entries.title: Cup No. 5
entries.text: A 4-1 win in Game 5 at Boston brings a fifth Cup in seven seasons, the first without Gretzky. Goalie Bill Ranford wins the Conn Smythe.

entries.title: Messier traded
entries.text: Captain Mark Messier is traded to the New York Rangers for Bernie Nicholls, Steven Rice and Louie DeBrusk.

entries.title: Marchant's Game 7 winner
entries.text: Todd Marchant scores at 12:26 of overtime in Game 7 as Edmonton upsets the Dallas Stars 4-3.

entries.title: Gretzky elected to the Hall
entries.text: Wayne Gretzky is unanimously elected to the Hockey Hall of Fame in the player category.

entries.title: No. 99 to the rafters
entries.text: The Oilers retire Gretzky's No. 99 before their season opener against the Rangers.

entries.title: The Heritage Classic
entries.text: The NHL's first regular-season outdoor game draws a record 57,167 to Commonwealth Stadium. Montreal edges Edmonton 4-3.

entries.title: Eighth seed topples Detroit
entries.text: Edmonton, the West's No. 8 seed, beats the top-seeded Red Wings 4-3 in Game 6 to win the series 4-2.

entries.title: Pisani's shorthanded OT winner
entries.text: Fernando Pisani scores the first shorthanded overtime goal in Final history, 3:31 into OT, as Edmonton wins Game 5 4-3 at Carolina.

entries.title: So close in Game 7
entries.text: The Oilers' run ends with a 3-1 loss to the Hurricanes in Game 7 of the Stanley Cup Final in Raleigh.

entries.title: Ten years without playoffs
entries.text: The Oilers miss the playoffs for 10 straight seasons, the stretch fans call the Decade of Darkness.

entries.title: Three straight No. 1 picks
entries.text: Edmonton picks first overall three years running: Taylor Hall (2010), Ryan Nugent-Hopkins (2011) and Nail Yakupov (2012).

entries.title: Lottery luck: McDavid
entries.text: Two months after jumping from third to first in the draft lottery, Edmonton selects Connor McDavid first overall from the Erie Otters.

entries.title: Farewell to the Coliseum
entries.text: The Oilers play their final game at Rexall Place, the old Northlands Coliseum, beating Vancouver 6-2.

entries.title: Youngest captain ever
entries.text: McDavid, 19 years and 266 days old, is named captain, the youngest in NHL history.

entries.title: Rogers Place opens
entries.text: The first regular-season game downtown is a 7-4 win over Calgary, with McDavid scoring twice.

entries.title: McDavid's first Hart
entries.text: McDavid wins the Art Ross Trophy with 100 points, plus the Hart Trophy and Ted Lindsay Award, as the Oilers return to the playoffs for the first time since 2006.

entries.title: Lowe makes seven
entries.text: Kevin Lowe is elected to the Hockey Hall of Fame, the seventh dynasty player inducted, joining Gretzky, Messier, Kurri, Coffey, Anderson and Fuhr.

entries.title: Draisaitl's Hart
entries.text: Leon Draisaitl leads the NHL with 110 points to win the Art Ross, Ted Lindsay and Hart, the first Germany-born Hart Trophy winner.

entries.title: A unanimous MVP
entries.text: McDavid scores 105 points in 56 games and wins the Hart with all 100 first-place votes, joining Gretzky as the only unanimous winners.

entries.title: Lowe's No. 4 retired
entries.text: Kevin Lowe's No. 4 joins Anderson, Coffey, Fuhr, Gretzky, Kurri and Messier in the rafters of Rogers Place.

entries.title: McDavid ends the Battle of Alberta
entries.text: McDavid scores in overtime of Game 5 for a 5-4 win that eliminates Calgary and sends Edmonton to the conference final for the first time since 2006.

entries.title: 64 goals, 153 points
entries.text: McDavid wins the Art Ross, Rocket Richard and Hart, with 64 goals and 153 points, the most points in a season since 1995-96.

entries.title: 16 straight wins
entries.text: Under new coach Kris Knoblauch (hired Nov 12, 2023), a 16-game winning streak ends in Vegas. It ties for the second-longest in NHL history, one short of Pittsburgh's record of 17.

entries.title: McDavid's 100 assists
entries.text: McDavid sets up Zach Hyman in a 9-2 win over San Jose to become the fourth player with 100 assists in a season, after Gretzky, Lemieux and Orr.

entries.title: Game 7 heartbreak
entries.text: After coming back from 3-0 down to force Game 7, the Oilers lose 2-1 in Florida. McDavid wins the Conn Smythe with 42 points, including a record 34 assists.

entries.title: McDavid's 1,000th point
entries.text: McDavid scores against Nashville to reach 1,000 points in his 659th game. Only Gretzky, Lemieux and Bossy got there faster.

entries.title: Rematch falls short
entries.text: After beating Dallas in five games to return to the Final, Edmonton falls 5-1 to Florida in Game 6, losing the Cup rematch.

entries.title: McDavid re-signs
entries.text: The captain signs a two-year extension with an average annual value of $12.5 million.

entries.title: Draisaitl hits 1,000
entries.text: Draisaitl becomes the first German player to reach 1,000 NHL points, in a 6-4 win over Pittsburgh.

entries.title: RNH's 1,000th game
entries.text: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins scores in his 1,000th NHL game, all with Edmonton, in a 5-0 win over St. Louis.

entries.title: McDavid's 400th goal
entries.text: McDavid scores twice at Utah for his 400th goal and 1,200th point, becoming the third-fastest player to 1,200 points.

entries.title: A sixth Art Ross
entries.text: McDavid wins the scoring title with 48 goals and 138 points, and has a point in all 41 Oilers wins.

entries.title: Out in Round 1
entries.text: Anaheim wins Game 6 5-2 to eliminate Edmonton 4-2 in the first round, the Oilers' earliest exit since 2021.

entries.title: Babcock takes over
entries.text: Six weeks after Kris Knoblauch is fired following three seasons and two Cup Final trips, Mike Babcock is hired as head coach.
